cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Reserve two chairs for her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.

mechanism: A corrects seating and identification for a guest and her future self, making B choose practical arrangements that assume both versions arrive.
confusable: D148 seeks formal approval; D155 only asks B to enact the impossible premise through an ordinary concrete choice.
comparison: Two versions of a family guest create hospitality labeling rather than a hungry-ceiling feeding task.
seedUse: Keep chair shortfall and future identification, but correct the actual arrangement rather than announce professionalism.
